study.research_question: Does adding personal coarse timing/image progress improve closed-loop control beyond shared personal geometry, with equal coverage and robot demo count?
study.teacher: same legacy initial-XY teacher; profile None versus matched personal timing/progress during transport only
study.collection_gate: Each group: all24 qualified lifts and >=20/24 strict successes; retain failures, no replacement or relaxed gate.
study.selection: same v6 learner, all3 fixed-final EMA models,2500 updates. Report all development cases and all fresh test cases; no best seed/checkpoint selection.
study.budget: 24 robot demonstrations each, exact paired scene/P/G/initial RGB, model init, sampling, augmentation, updates. Lengths/frame targets/compute may differ.
study.information_boundary: current RGB +12D robot/preprovided goal/past command only; no runtime object truth, clock, phase, or human profile
study.fresh_test_scope: 32 tasks over8 physical object starts, repeated for3 model seeds; same simulator family, not96 independent environments
limitations: Prior coverage and S01 timing results informed this design: exploratory new comparison.
Personal labels are RGB candidates and Codex coarse visual brackets, not human-annotated physical actions.
X03 previously viewed for naming/QC; no X03 trajectory extraction, tuning or training in this study.
This comparison tests coarse timing+progress, not a pure timing or pure progress intervention.
